Spawn options, persistent output streaming, lifecycle hardening, timestamped capture, the interactive sample, MiniPty.Console (use case 3), and the editor terminal backend (use case 4) are implemented. See [specs/core_session.md](specs/core_session.md), [specs/lifecycle.md](specs/lifecycle.md), [specs/capture.md](specs/capture.md), [specs/console.md](specs/console.md), [specs/terminal.md](specs/terminal.md).

GUI host readiness is implemented, and its plan is retired: caller-context safety and thread-pool independence ([Caller context](specs/core_session.md#caller-context)), exit-tolerant resize, platform size limits, GUI host guidance with WinUI 3 and Avalonia samples ([GUI hosts](specs/core_session.md#gui-hosts)), bounded end of output on Windows, explicit Unix termios with `IUTF8`, hang-up before kill on Unix dispose, the opt-in out-of-band ConPTY with `Clear()` ([Out-of-band ConPTY](specs/core_session.md#out-of-band-conpty)), opt-in process-tree cleanup ([Process tree](specs/core_session.md#process-tree)), bounded UI-thread occupancy during output floods, and child-`PATH` program lookup on Windows ([Program lookup](specs/core_session.md#program-lookup-windows)). Its lessons live in those specifications and in [platform_support.md](specs/platform_support.md), [pty_crossplatform.md](references/pty_crossplatform.md), and [gui_terminal_samples.md](references/gui_terminal_samples.md).

**Next:** [Thread-free I/O](plans/plan_thread_free_io.md) is in progress for web hosts that keep many sessions open: Phases 0 and 1 are done and measured on Windows, Linux, and macOS; Phase 2 (the output pump driven through an output-driver contract) and Phase 3 (one-shot sinks that cost the same on any delivering thread) are done, and the full suite passed on macOS too; Phase 4 chose `kqueue` for the macOS and FreeBSD loop (probed on macOS, from source for FreeBSD); Phase 5 (the Windows engine) is done on Windows, where sessions now read through I/O completions and an idle session holds no thread and no output buffer, and the full suite with it passed on macOS; Phase 6 (the Unix engine) is done on Linux and macOS, where one loop reads every session (epoll, kqueue), and FreeBSD runs the same kqueue code from source; on macOS a flood through the WebSocket bridge took about 33 frames per 32 KiB instead of 8, and was about 12% slower, and Phase 7 (the bridges join output that arrives in a burst into larger chunks, while the session still publishes each read as it completes) brought it to 4 frames per 32 KiB and faster than with reader threads, measured on macOS so far, with Windows and Linux next; Phase 8 then decides whether the bridges join steady output below the burst rate, and Phase 9 retires the reader threads. Phase 1 also fixed a pre-existing race in the output pump that could end a session and lose its remaining output under a flood, Phase 4 found that macOS discarded a child's last output at its exit when the consumer had stopped reading, which a slave descriptor the session now holds there prevents, and Phase 3 fixed a Phase 1 regression in which `CompleteAsync` and Capture with `DecodeOutput` threw when several reads had piled up before the sink attached. What else is left is listed below. Remaining deferred and won't-do node-pty parity items are recorded as non-goals in [specs/terminal.md](specs/terminal.md).

## Release

- None of the GUI host work is released. `v1.3.0` (2026-07-15) predates it, and `Directory.Build.props` still says `1.3.0`.
- The release breaks the API: `WaitForExitAsync` returns `Task<PtyExitStatus>`, and `WaitForExitStatusAsync` is removed. Behavior a release note should name: `Dispose` no longer blocks, and chunk memory is invalid after it; output is read from spawn into a bounded 16 KiB buffer, and a `ReadOutputAsync` chunk is all the contiguous output buffered when it is taken (up to 16 KiB), not one read; exit waits no longer close the transport, so on the in-box ConPTY before Windows 11 24H2 output ends about 100 ms after the last output rather than at exit (from 24H2 it ends at exit, as on the out-of-band ConPTY); `Resize` after exit no longer throws, and sizes clamp to the platform limit instead of 512; Unix `Dispose` hangs the child up and kills it one second later instead of killing at once; `SendEof` with no input sends Ctrl+Z + CR instead of closing the pipe; on Windows a `.bat` or `.cmd` runs through `cmd.exe` with its arguments escaped, and a bare `FileName` is looked up on the child's `PATH` when `Environment` sets or removes it; `Pty.Start` throws `ArgumentException` for a NUL in `FileName`, an argument, `WorkingDirectory`, or `CommandLine` on every platform, where it used to start whatever the string named before the NUL; on Windows a program under a path of 260 characters or more starts when the host opted into long paths, where it used to fail with `ERROR_FILENAME_EXCED_RANGE`; on macOS a child that exits while its last output is still in the terminal, because the output buffer is full, finishes exiting once a consumer reads, where macOS used to discard up to 1 KiB of that output 0.6 s after the exit; on Windows output is read through I/O completions on the runtime's thread pool instead of a reader thread per session, so an idle session holds no thread and no output buffer, chunks are no longer held for a 500 µs coalescing window, and the `MiniPty.UseOutputReaderThreads` `AppContext` switch restores the reader threads as a temporary rollback.
- The README samples under `samples/SingleFiles` (`README_MiniPty.cs`, `README_MiniPty.Console.cs`, `README_MiniPty.Capture.cs`) pin `MiniPty@1.2.0`, but the first two already use the new exit API (`(await session.WaitForExitAsync()).ExitCode`), so they do not build until the pins move to the release. CI does not build them.

## Deferred Until an Embedder Needs It

### Unix disposal grace as an option

The one-second hang-up grace before the kill (`UnixPtyBackend.DisposeHangupGraceMs`) is fixed. It can become an option if an embedder needs a different one.

## Unverified

- **`ClosePseudoConsole` on older Windows builds.** On build 26200 it returned within 1 ms in every measured session, also while an unrelated process held the output pipe open. Whether it can block on Windows 10, or on Windows 11 before 24H2, while output is not drained is not verified; disposal switches the reader to discarding output before the close for that reason. If it can block, `Dispose` must close off the calling thread and `DisposeAsync` must include the close in its wait. Also unverified: whether, on a build where the close waits for the console host, a process that inherited the output pipe keeps that host alive and makes the close wait for it too.
- **Minimum macOS version of the native binaries.** `scripts/build-native.sh` passes no `-mmacosx-version-min`, and no workflow sets `MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET`, so `libminipty_unix.dylib`, the static archive, and `minipty_spawn_helper` declare the build host's macOS as their minimum (`minos 26.0` in `otool -l`), and the release builds them on `macos-26` runners. Linking a NativeAOT sample against the archive warns about it. Whether an older macOS refuses to load them was not tested.
- **FreeBSD** is tested neither locally nor in CI. Its termios (`VERASE2`, and `_POSIX_VDISABLE` being 0xff), its reader wake pipe, whether it revokes the tty when the session leader exits, as macOS does, and the readiness behavior Phase 4 chose `kqueue` on, which the Unix loop now reads every session with, follow from source only. `scripts/pty-readiness-probe.c` checks the readiness part where a FreeBSD machine is available.
- **Host exit on macOS under NativeAOT.** A host that disposes a session whose child ignores `SIGHUP` and then exits sends the pending kill at exit. On macOS that was probed under CoreCLR and NativeAOT with an earlier version that armed a timer per disposal, not with the current exit-watcher deadline; CI runs the CoreCLR test (`HostExitKillsAChildStillInItsHangupGrace`) there.
- **Output buffer geometry.** 4 slots × 4 KiB was chosen because every allocation benchmark improved with it, and 32 KiB from ConPTY arrives in 12–13 chunks. Throughput has not been tuned.

## Rare Test Timeouts Under Heavy Load

- **Windows:** in `QueuedInputIsDeliveredInOrderWithEofAfterItWhileOutputIsBackedUp`, a blocking write issued behind a queue that had stayed pending for 500 ms completed within 100 ms once in 11 runs of the EOF tests under 3× CPU oversubscription on a desktop, before `SendEof` was called: the console host took input for a moment while its output was still backed up, so the test's premise did not hold and the EOF path was not involved. Not seen on hosted runners since the flood tests were reworked.
- **macOS:** `SendEofEndsInputAfterACanceledWriteLeftAPartialLine` timed out once in 48 full-suite runs with 64 busy processes on 8 cores, and once in 20 such runs before an earlier round of fixes. It passed 84 later runs with about 128 busy processes, alone, with its class, or with the suite. The cause is not known.
